blocks.title: The modern periodic law
blocks.text: The physical and chemical properties of elements are periodic functions of their atomic numbers.

The atomic number is the number of protons in an atom. The law is the cornerstone of the periodic table: elements with similar properties appear at certain intervals. When the elements are arranged by increasing atomic number, sodium, potassium and cesium show many physical and chemical characteristics similar to lithium, because they all fall in the same group. But because the number of protons in the nucleus rises gradually and new electron shells are added, the physical and chemical properties of elements vary systematically within a group and within a period. The following topics take the properties one by one: atomic radius, ionic radius, ionization energy, electron affinity, electronegativity and metallic character.

blocks.alt: A grey rectangle stands for the periodic table. A green arrow across the top and a green arrow up the right side carry the properties that increase across a period and up a group; blue arrows across the bottom and down the left carry atomic radius and metallic character. Corner notes name cesium and francium as most metallic and fluorine as most electronegative.
blocks.caption: The periodic trends at a glance (original diagram after Figures 1.9 and 1.3).
blocks.long_description: Across a period from left to right, ionization energy, electron affinity, electronegativity and non-metallic character increase, while atomic radius and metallic character decrease; down a group, atomic radius and metallic character increase while ionization energy, electron affinity and electronegativity decrease. The most metallic elements are at the bottom left and the most electronegative at the top right. Every trend follows from the effective nuclear charge felt by the valence electrons and the number of shells beneath them.
